blocks.text: The module documentation defines read, list, edit, write, and delete behavior, caps, symlink rules, seen-file requirements, and crash-safe temporary-file handling.
blocks.title: Filesystem tool guarantees

blocks.text: SeenRecord stores metadata and an optional hash. SeenFiles maintains a bounded, thread-safe insertion-ordered map and supports recording, lookup, forgetting, and containment checks.
blocks.title: Seen-file state

blocks.text: Helpers sanitize displayed names, map OS errors to stable ToolErrors, normalize guarded wrappers, read bounded bytes, decode UTF-8 text, split lines, and format numbered output.
blocks.title: Read and error helpers

blocks.text: read_file resolves and opens a regular file without following its final symlink, hashes normal-sized content into seen state, and streams oversized files. Rendering applies line and output caps with continuation markers.
blocks.title: Reading files

blocks.anchor: def list_dir(ctx: ToolContext, path: str = ".", max_depth: int = 1) -> tuple[str, bool]:
blocks.text: list_dir walks bounded depth with directories first, hides denied entries, labels safe symlinks without exposing outside targets, and stops at the entry cap.
blocks.title: Directory listing

blocks.anchor: def _load_for_change(ctx, pfd: int, name: str, real_path) -> tuple[bytes, os.stat_result, str]:
blocks.text: Existing files are loaded whole only within the size cap and must have a matching SeenRecord hash. This establishes the before-state required by edit and overwrite operations.
blocks.title: Pre-write consistency

blocks.text: The writer handles short writes, process liveness, stale temporary files, last-moment target verification, same-directory replacement, directory fsync, and seen-state refresh.
blocks.title: Atomic write machinery

blocks.text: edit_file requires an exact old-string match and returns a capped unified diff. write_file validates UTF-8 content, enforces caps and prior-read checks, then uses the atomic writer.
blocks.title: Edit and write operations

gotchas: Large files can be read but cannot be edited or overwritten.
write_file requires a prior read for existing files.
Recursive deletion is available to this Python function but not exposed by the protocol schema.
purpose: This module is the filesystem tool layer for a session-scoped project root. It resolves paths through the path guard, caps output and writes, records read hashes before edits, avoids following final symlinks, and performs atomic same-directory replacement with concurrent-change checks.
summary: Implements guarded file listing, reading, editing, atomic writing, stale-temp cleanup, and deletion tools.

params.desc: Content hash or None for oversized files
params.name: sha256
